title: Open-window fairshare fallback & circuit playbook
creator: Sasha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket defines an operational and implementation playbook for handling large, multi-tenant bursts under partial or full limiter outages across regions. It combines an 'open-window' sliding fairshare reservoir (local fast-path) with hedged cross-region reconciliation and a deterministic circuit policy that biases toward preserving SLOs for high-priority customers. The goal is to make burst absorption graceful, predictable, and auditable while minimizing tail-latency regressions and unfair starvation during degraded limiter availability.

Background and motivation: We continue to see two failure classes that cause production impact: (1) limiter control-plane or datastore outages that make centralized quota decisions unavailable, and (2) extreme correlated bursts (e.g., release-day traffic or tenant storms) that outstrip steady-state quotas. Existing mitigations (static emergency quotas and global fallback to permissive mode) either cause unfairness (first-come-first-serve bursts) or excessive SLO violations for critical customers. We need a cohesive approach that: preserves latency SLOs where possible; enforces predictable prioritization; degrades smoothly rather than flapping; and is operationally simple to observe and recover.

Design overview: The playbook has three cooperating components:
1) Local open-window fairshare reservoir (fast-path): a lightweight in-memory sliding-window reservoir per instance that grants short-term burst credits proportional to tenant weight. Credits are replenished on a rolling time-window (configurable, default 30s) and are conservatively seeded from the last-known global allocation when available. The reservoir is designed to operate without cross-region coordination for O(100ms) decision latency.
2) Hedged cross-region reconciliation (background): a periodic, eventual reconciliation process (default 1s cadence) that exchanges compact digests of in-use credits (hash + counters) between regions. When connectivity allows, regions rebalance long-running credit skews by transferring ledger deltas or by instructing local instances to adjust drain rates. During reconciliation failures, local reservoirs continue to operate independently with conservative safety margins.
3) Deterministic circuit policy & emergency shedding: a top-level circuit that transitions to three states: CLOSED (normal enforcement), SOFT_OPEN (aggressive shedding of low-weight tenants while preserving high-weight SLO allocations), and HARD_OPEN (global emergency cap with even stricter proportional enforcement). Transitions are driven by a combination of metrics: global token_headroom_ratio, cross-region reconciliation latency, limiter write errors, and SLO miss rate per priority bucket. The circuit uses hysteresis windows and exponential backoff to prevent oscillation.

Key behavioral guarantees and tradeoffs: 
- Fairness: short bursts are proportional to configured tenant weights using a token-bucket-like apportionment over the open window. This preserves relative fairness versus FCFS.
- SLO preservation: high-priority tenants have reserved baseline allocations which are honored even under SOFT_OPEN unless physical capacity is exhausted.
- Latency: local reservoir fast-path minimizes decision latency. Hedged reconciliation is background and does not affect request-critical paths.
- Cost vs strictness: seeding reservoirs conservatively reduces oversubscription but increases false-negative shedding (higher request rejections during transients). The default safety margin is 10% of last-known capacity; this is tunable per deployment.

Implementation notes:
- Data model: per-tenant ledger entries: last_replenish_ts, window_tokens_remaining, weight, lease_epoch. Stored in local memory with periodic snapshot to a local ephemeral store (Redis/LDB) for recovery. Snapshots are compact (TTL 60s).
- Reconciliation protocol: use compact protobuf digest with incremental deltas to avoid full state transfer; backoff on conflict and conflict-resolution by epoch. Utilize existing lease token scheme from ENG-27183 to minimize races.
- Circuit signals: implement metrics ingestion (Datadog/Prometheus) for token_headroom_ratio, limiter_error_rate, reconciliation_lag_ms, slo_violation_rate_by_priority. Circuit state machine lives in the control-plane with a small authoritative decision service; per-region agents subscribe to state changes and implement local enforcement.
- Observability: dashboards for: per-tenant burst_headroom, shed_rate_by_priority, replenish_rate, reservoir_fill_percent, reconciliation_success_rate. Create SLO-specific charts showing 'requests_served_within_slo' vs 'requests_shed' by priority.

Simulation and validation plan:
1) Unit tests for reservoir arithmetic (drain/replenish), deterministic fairness property with synthetic tenants.
2) Integration tests in staging with region failure simulation (partition one region, cut control-plane, generate synthetic bursts across tenants).
3) Chaos experiments: (a) limiter datastore latency injection, (b) delayed reconciliation messages, (c) restart of a subset of regional agents to test re-seeding/snapshots. Capture SLOs and fairness metrics.

Rollout and roll-back strategy:
- Phase 1 (Canary): deploy local reservoir fast-path with no circuit transitions (monitor only) to 5% of traffic in one non-critical region. Run 2 weeks of baseline and burst tests.
- Phase 2 (Controlled): enable SOFT_OPEN only for test tenants and internal customers; expose dashboards and create alert threshold fine-tuning.
- Phase 3 (Broad): enable for all traffic with HARD_OPEN thresholds set conservatively. Monitor for 1 week, then tighten thresholds if stable.
- Rollback: control-plane can force CLOSED state globally; agents accept a force-closed signal with immediate reservoir drain. Automatically roll back if SLO violation exceeds 2x baseline for >10 minutes.

Operational playbook (runbook snippets):
- When reconciliation_lag_ms > 1500ms for > 1m: set circuit to SOFT_OPEN for affected regions and notify network/infra.
- If limiter_error_rate spikes > 5% and token_headroom_ratio < 0.2: escalate to SRE lead, set HARD_OPEN with temporary reserved capacity for 'critical' customers.
- Post-incident: collect reservoir snapshots, reconciliation digests, and Datadog trace for the 5 minutes prior to transition; create postmortem with mitigation timeline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests pass in CI.
- Staging chaos tests show SLO preservation for high-priority tenants (>=99.9% within SLO) while low-priority shed_rate < 25% across simulated storm scenarios.
- Dashboards instrumented and alerting thresholds validated.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Open-Window+Fairshare+Playbook
- Staging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2842
- Simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/tree/main/fairshare-reservoir

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Determine default safety margin for seeding (10% is a starting point; run experiments to optimize).
- Define SLA for reconciliation latency under various network conditions.
- Mapping of tenant weights to SLO reservation tiers — need PM input to avoid mispriced guarantees.
